Conflict: Material and Design recommends PCR PP monomaterial for circularity, whereas In-Service rejects this because PCR PP has lower impact strength and scratch resistance compared to high-impact virgin ABS/PC.
Decision: Post-consumer recycled (PCR) Polypropylene (PP) monomaterial with molded-in textures
Rationale: While virgin ABS/PC offers higher impact resistance, PCR PP significantly reduces the carbon footprint and is highly recyclable. Mechanical durability will be addressed through optimized structural ribbing and wall thickness, balancing engineering feasibility with sustainability best practice.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: material circularity vs mechanical durability

Conflict: Circularity recommends snap-fits and removable screws for easy disassembly, whereas In-Service demands threaded fasteners with brass inserts for repeated repair durability, and Manufacture prefers pure snap-fits to avoid secondary assembly steps.
Decision: Reversible snap-fits and standardized removable metal screws
Rationale: This option avoids permanent metal inserts (brass) which contaminate plastic recycling streams, while still allowing non-destructive disassembly for repair, unlike pure snap-fits which are highly prone to shearing during servicing.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: ease of disassembly vs joint durability under vibration

Conflict: Circularity recommends a modular BLDC motor with mechanically fastened magnets for recycling, while In-Service recommends a standard high-efficiency BLDC motor for performance, and Manufacture recommends a ferrite-magnet motor to avoid rare-earth mining impacts.
Decision: Modular BLDC motor with mechanically fastened rare-earth magnets and slide-out copper stator
Rationale: This ensures the high power density and efficiency required for vacuum performance (engineering feasibility) while allowing the non-destructive recovery of critical rare-earth magnets and copper at end-of-life (sustainability best practice).
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: critical raw material recovery vs use-phase energy efficiency

Conflict: In-Service recommends an active bypass cooling fan to prevent thermal degradation of the motor, whereas Material and Circularity recommend passive cooling to reduce weight and avoid unrecyclable potting compounds.
Decision: Bypass active cooling fan integrated with main suction airflow and removable aluminum fins
Rationale: Passive cooling is insufficient for high-power, compact vacuum motors, making active cooling an engineering necessity. Using removable aluminum fins avoids unrecyclable potting compounds and allows clean material separation at end-of-life.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: thermal reliability vs material simplicity

Conflict: Manufacture recommends a monolithic integrated design to minimize tooling energy and scrap, whereas In-Service and Circularity demand a modular architecture with user-replaceable parts to facilitate repair and extend product life.
Decision: Modular architecture with tool-less user-replaceable battery, motor, and filter cartridges
Rationale: Extending the product's useful life through easy repair has a significantly lower overall lifecycle environmental impact than minimizing initial manufacturing tooling complexity, aligning with sustainability best practices.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing simplicity vs repairability and lifetime extension

Conflict: Manufacture recommends corded AC power to completely eliminate battery manufacturing footprints, whereas In-Service and Circularity recommend a removable battery pack to provide cordless portability while ensuring the battery is replaceable.
Decision: Removable and modular Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery pack
Rationale: While corded power has a lower manufacturing footprint, cordless operation is a critical market requirement. LFP chemistry avoids toxic cobalt and nickel (substances of concern) and offers a significantly longer cycle life than standard Li-ion.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing footprint of energy storage vs use-phase portability
